name: Rowing machine
pattern: Seated full-body pull: legs push, the body swings back from the hips, then the arms pull, and the return goes in reverse order.
setup: Strap your feet so the strap crosses the widest part of the foot.
Damper at 3-5: higher feels heavier but is not a better workout.
Hold the handle with a loose overhand grip, wrists flat.

steps.text: At the front: shins near vertical, arms long, body tipped forward from the hips (about 1 o'clock).
Push the footplate away with your legs. Arms stay straight and the back keeps its angle.
Legs flat, lean back to about 11 o'clock, pull the handle to your lower ribs.
Straighten your arms first, then tip your body forward from the hips.
Once the handle passes your knees, bend them and slide forward slowly to the catch.

cues.cue: Legs, body, arms. Then arms, body, legs.
cues.why: The legs make most of the power; arms pulling early lose it and the handle path breaks.

cues.cue: Hinge at the hips, chest proud, do not slump at the catch.
cues.why: Lumbar flexion at the catch is about 15° in elite rowers and it grows with fatigue, which is linked to back pain.

cues.cue: Drive fast, return slow: about 1 count out, 2 counts back.
cues.why: Rushing the slide makes you arrive at the catch in a poor position and wastes energy.

cues.cue: Stop the slide when the shins are vertical.
cues.why: Going further cramps the hips and lets the back round.

cues.cue: Shoulders low, elbows draw back past the ribs.
cues.why: Shrugging tires the neck and adds nothing to the stroke.

breathing: Out on the drive, in on the recovery. At high rates add a quick breath at the finish.

tempo.note: Drive about 1/3 of the stroke, recovery 2/3. Steady rowing 18-24 strokes a minute.

mistakes.name: Arms bend early
mistakes.looks: The elbows bend before the legs are flat.
mistakes.fix: Arms long like ropes until the handle passes your knees.
mistakes.why: The small arm muscles take the load the legs should carry.

mistakes.name: Back rounds at the catch
mistakes.looks: The lower back slumps and the head drops as you reach forward.
mistakes.fix: Tip forward from the hips with a long spine; reach less if you must.
mistakes.why: Rounding grows as you tire and puts the load on the lower back.

mistakes.name: Rushed slide
mistakes.looks: You shoot back up the slide as fast as you drove.
mistakes.fix: Count 1 on the drive, 1-2 on the way back.
mistakes.why: It raises effort, shortens the stroke and makes the next catch weak.

mistakes.name: Leaning too far back
mistakes.looks: Shoulders well behind the hips at the finish.
mistakes.why: Extra lean adds little length and strains the back and abs.

safety: Lower-back pain: shorten the reach at the catch and keep the damper low.
Rib pain in heavy training can be a stress fracture; stop and get it checked.

metrics.label: Body angle
metrics.good: 20 to 30 forward at catch, 20 to 35 back at finish

motion.basis: Lumbar flexion at the catch (about 15°) from fohanno2015; the clock-face trunk angles (±25-30°) and 1:2 rhythm are Concept2 coaching convention. Hip, knee, ankle and arm angles are estimates from the seat and handle geometry.
